answer: Divergent-Response Identity Test. Each identity must answer randomized challenges whose correct answers depend on its private history, and a trellis of peers cross-checks responses for consistency. A clone farm sharing one controller cannot make members diverge independently, so any coordinated answer produces an echo across the group, flagged as correlated. Honest agents pay only compute; attackers must supply genuinely separate histories and independent decision paths per identity, a delta of real cost that scales linearly and cannot be copied.
